title: The Economics of Old Friends
sentences: Long friendships run on a currency that is genuinely difficult to acquire later in life.
They contain a shared record that neither party ever has to stop and summarise aloud.
You can begin a sentence somewhere in the middle and still be understood.
Newer friendships, however warm they are, require constant explanation of the background.
This is exactly why people describe old friends as restful rather than especially exciting company.
The cost is that the record includes versions of you that you had long ago abandoned.
Old friends are the last people still holding the earlier drafts of your character.
Some of us find that deeply reassuring and others find it quietly rather confining.
Both reactions are perfectly reasonable, and they often occur in the very same person.
What cannot be manufactured at any speed at all is the accumulated time the friendship rests on.
